name: glycolysis
description: Glycolysis – the central pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate (or lactate under anaerobic conditions). Modeled from the book pathway chart.

nodes.label: Glucose
nodes.notes: Starting substrate. Blood glucose enters the cell via GLUT transporters.

nodes.label: Glucose-6-phosphate
nodes.notes: First committed intermediate. Traps glucose inside the cell.

nodes.label: Fructose-6-phosphate
nodes.notes: Isomer of G6P. Substrate for the major regulatory enzyme PFK-1.

nodes.label: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate
nodes.notes: Product of the committed step. Split into two triose phosphates.

nodes.label: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate
nodes.notes: One of the two trioses produced by aldolase. Rapidly isomerized to GAP.

nodes.label: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
nodes.notes: The triose that continues through the payoff phase. Two molecules per glucose.

nodes.label: 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate
nodes.notes: High-energy intermediate. Contains a mixed anhydride capable of substrate-level phosphorylation.

nodes.label: 3-Phosphoglycerate
nodes.notes: Product of the first substrate-level phosphorylation (ATP generation).

nodes.label: 2-Phosphoglycerate
nodes.notes: Isomer of 3-PG. Prepared for dehydration to PEP.

nodes.label: Phosphoenolpyruvate
nodes.notes: Highest-energy phosphate compound in glycolysis. Drives the second ATP-forming step.

nodes.label: Pyruvate
nodes.notes: End product of aerobic glycolysis. Can enter mitochondria (PDH → acetyl-CoA) or be reduced to lactate.

nodes.label: Lactate
nodes.notes: Anaerobic end product. Regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue when oxygen is limited.

edges.notes: First ATP investment. Irreversible under physiological conditions. Traps glucose in the cell.
Reversible isomerization. Prepares the molecule for the next phosphorylation.
Second ATP investment. The committed step of glycolysis. Highly regulated.
Cleaves the 6-carbon sugar into two 3-carbon units (DHAP + GAP).
Same reaction produces the second triose (GAP).
Rapidly converts DHAP into GAP so both trioses can proceed through the payoff phase. Near-equilibrium reaction.
Oxidative step. Uses NAD⁺ and inorganic phosphate. Produces the high-energy mixed anhydride 1,3-BPG and one NADH. This is the only redox step in glycolysis.
First substrate-level phosphorylation. Transfers the high-energy phosphate to ADP → ATP.
Reversible relocation of the phosphate group from carbon 3 to carbon 2.
Dehydration reaction that creates the high-energy enol phosphate PEP.
Second substrate-level phosphorylation. Generates the second pair of ATP molecules and produces pyruvate.

Anaerobic regeneration of NAD⁺. Allows glycolysis to continue when oxygen (and therefore the electron transport chain) is limited. Lactate can later be converted back to glucose in the liver (Cori cycle).
